rulings.ruling: Ruling: second transcription right in part; proposed finding (the box changes no amount). i2441 p. 3, Column (c): "Check the box in column (c) if the qualifying person listed in column (a) was over age 12 at the time the care was provided and was disabled." The project checks the box for every qualifying person not able to care for themselves except a qualifying child under 13 all year (`dependent.dc_child_all_year` false), so a qualifying person under 13 who is not your qualifying child but qualifies through the disabled route (for example an unrelated child aged 10 who lived with you all year as a member of your household, your dependent as a qualifying relative, and not able to care for themselves) is checked though never over age 12; the second leaves it unchecked. Proposed fix: replace the `dependent.dc_child_all_year == false` test with the age, `dependent.age` not less than `dc.child_age` (13 or over at the end of 2025). The second also leaves the box unchecked for a disabled qualifying child who turned 13 in 2025 (its note); there the project is retained: care given after the 13th birthday was given while the child was over age 12 and disabled, and column (c) adds "A person over age 12 at the time the care was provided must be physically or mentally incapable of caring for themselves to be listed on line 2", which is that child's position for that care. Fixed during integration (BUG-0080): `dependent.dc_line2c` now tests the person's age against `dc.child_age` (13) instead of `dependent.dc_child_all_year`.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained (as the prior ruling; the box changes no amount). i2441 p. 3, Column (c): 'Check the box in column (c) if the qualifying person listed in column (a) was over age 12 at the time the care was provided and was disabled.' The project checks it for a qualifying person who is not able to care for themselves and is 13 or older at the end of 2025; the second writes the qualifying-person test in its own structure. The one case the box could differ, a disabled child who turned 13 in 2025 and had care only before the birthday, is not asked and changes no amount.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: reading; project retained (the box changes no amount). After BUG-0080's fix the sides differ only for a disabled qualifying child who turned 13 during 2025: the project checks the box (age 13 or more at the end of 2025, unable to care for themselves), the second checks it only for a person not under 13 for any part of 2025. i2441 p. 3, Column (c): "Check the box in column (c) if the qualifying person listed in column (a) was over age 12 at the time the care was provided and was disabled"; the care after the birthday counts only through the disability rule (i2441 p. 1, Qualifying Person(s), "If the child turned 13 during the year, the child is a qualifying person for the part of the year they were under age 13"), so the person listed was over age 12 and disabled for that care. Listed for the owner as a display reading.

The project checks it for a qualifying person who is not able to care for themselves and is 13 or older at the end of 2025; the second writes the qualifying-person test in its own structure. The one case the box could differ, a disabled child who turned 13 in 2025 and had care only before the birthday, is not asked and changes no amount.

The total is the same; the benefits reading is the register's (amb.2025.dc_line30).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The second zeroes column (d) for an entry that is not a qualifying person; the project shows the entry's expenses and the line 3 total `f2441.paid_total` sums column (d) only over the dependents with `dependent.dc_qp` true, so no amount on the form differs (i2441 p. 3, Line 2, "Don't list a person on line 2 unless they are listed as an eligible person under Qualifying Person(s)"). The second's note leaves the Part III benefits to lines 29 to 31, which is the binding reading `amb.2025.dc_line30` (column (d) before excluding benefits; i2441 p. 3, Column (d), "If you completed Part III, don't include in column (d) any benefits shown on line 28"); 2024 expenses paid in 2025 are refused on line 9b (`f2441.prior_year`), which the project's column (d) need not read since the input excludes them ("Do not include 2024 care paid in 2025"; i2441 p. 3, Column (d), "Expenses you incurred in 2024 but didn't pay until 2025. Instead, see the instructions for line 9b").

The project copies the person's qualified expenses and applies the qualifying-person test where column (d) is summed (f2441.paid_total, 'where dependent.dc_qp'); the second zeroes the column for a person who is not a qualifying person (i2441 p. 3, Line 2, "Don't list a person on line 2 unless they are listed as an eligible person under Qualifying Person(s), earlier"). The total is the same; the benefits reading is the register's (amb.2025.dc_line30).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope and representation; project retained. The second transcription folds the qualifying-child, dependency and credit tests into each line; it also lets the rule for children of divorced or separated parents stand in for residency and omits the 'you can be claimed as a dependent' condition (`sa.dependent`), both refused in scope (`dependent.divorced_rule` refuses the entry; `sa.dependent` refuses the standard deduction). Compared by sampling 40,000 inputs per line with every refusal trigger false and consistent answers (only a married person files a joint return; over half of a person's support cannot come from both the person and you): no difference on the child tax credit lines; the remaining differences on odc_person, odc_amount and hoh_test2 all come from the second treating `sibling_descendant` as a Step 4 relative, which the enum defines as any other descendant of a sibling (a Step 4 relative only as a household member who lived with you all year; i1040gi p. 19 lists only a son or daughter of a sibling, which is `sibling`), and from `other` living with you all year, which the all-year household bullet admits. No change. Stage 13 re-run: the second transcription now applies the joint-return identification rules as the project does (household.ctc_ssn, household.all_tin, household.all_work_ssn; i1040gi p. 17, Before you begin, and p. 40, Step 1, question 2).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope and representation; project retained. The second transcription folds the qualifying-child, dependency and credit tests into each line; it also lets the rule for children of divorced or separated parents stand in for residency and omits the 'you can be claimed as a dependent' condition (`sa.dependent`), both refused in scope (`dependent.divorced_rule` refuses the entry; `sa.dependent` refuses the standard deduction). Compared by sampling 40,000 inputs per line with every refusal trigger false and consistent answers (only a married person files a joint return; over half of a person's support cannot come from both the person and you): no difference on the child tax credit lines; the remaining differences on odc_person, odc_amount and hoh_test2 all come from the second treating `sibling_descendant` as a Step 4 relative, which the enum defines as any other descendant of a sibling (a Step 4 relative only as a household member who lived with you all year; i1040gi p. 19 lists only a son or daughter of a sibling, which is `sibling`), and from `other` living with you all year, which the all-year household bullet admits. No change. Stage 13 re-run: the second transcription now applies the joint-return identification rules as the project does (household.ctc_ssn, household.all_tin, household.all_work_ssn; i1040gi p. 17, Before you begin, and p. 40, Step 1, question 2).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope and representation; project retained. Both read the household answer `f2441.care` (the second's note), the dependency tests, and the two routes of i2441 p. 1, Qualifying Person(s): "A qualifying child under age 13 whom you can claim as a dependent. If the child turned 13 during the year, the child is a qualifying person for the part of the year they were under age 13" and "Any disabled person who wasn't physically or mentally able to care for themselves who lived with you for more than half the year and whom you can claim as a dependent". The second asks `dependent.dc_under13` of every qualifying child; the project derives it from the age (under 13 at the end of 2025 is under 13 all year, 14 or over never under 13) and asks it only at 13. It also omits `sa.dependent`, refused in scope. Sampling 40,000 inputs per line with every refusal trigger false (`dependent.other_claimant`, `.divorced_rule`, `.multiple_support`, `.married`, `.income_exception`, `sa.dependent`) and consistent answers (only a married person files a joint return; over half of a person's support cannot come from both the person and you), and `dc_under13` answered consistently with the age: the only differences are the dependency-test differences ruled on dependent.odc_person (`sibling_descendant` living with you less than all year, `other` living with you all year), where the project follows i1040gi p. 19, Step 4. No change.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. Following the helper label, the second transcription adds 'lives with you no more than half the year' to Test 1; the project reads only the question 'For a parent not living with you, you paid over half the cost of their main home for all of 2025?'. They differ only when that question is answered yes for a parent who lives with you; such a dependent parent qualifies the filer through Test 2, item 1 (hoh_test2 admits a claimed parent who lived with you more than half the year), so head of household eligibility is the same. Sampling (40,000 inputs, refusal triggers false) finds no other difference.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. Test 1 (i1040gi p. 14): 'You paid over half the cost of keeping up a home that was the main home for all of 2025 of your parent whom you can claim as a dependent ... Your parent didn't have to live with you.' The project tests the parent value, the dependent line (now carrying the TIN refusal) and dependent.parent_home_paid; the second adds a residence test ('does not live with you', read as not more than half of 2025) that the text does not impose; a parent who did live with you also qualifies under Test 2, so the head of household result is the same.

The second writes the same exclusions in its own structure.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope and representation; project retained. The second transcription folds the qualifying-child, dependency and credit tests into each line; it also lets the rule for children of divorced or separated parents stand in for residency and omits the 'you can be claimed as a dependent' condition (`sa.dependent`), both refused in scope (`dependent.divorced_rule` refuses the entry; `sa.dependent` refuses the standard deduction). Compared by sampling 40,000 inputs per line with every refusal trigger false and consistent answers (only a married person files a joint return; over half of a person's support cannot come from both the person and you): no difference on the child tax credit lines; the remaining differences on odc_person, odc_amount and hoh_test2 all come from the second treating `sibling_descendant` as a Step 4 relative, which the enum defines as any other descendant of a sibling (a Step 4 relative only as a household member who lived with you all year; i1040gi p. 19 lists only a son or daughter of a sibling, which is `sibling`), and from `other` living with you all year, which the all-year household bullet admits. No change. Stage 13 re-run: the second transcription now applies the joint-return identification rules as the project does (household.ctc_ssn, household.all_tin, household.all_work_ssn; i1040gi p. 17, Before you begin, and p. 40, Step 1, question 2).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope and representation; project retained. The second transcription folds the qualifying-child, dependency and credit tests into each line; it also lets the rule for children of divorced or separated parents stand in for residency and omits the 'you can be claimed as a dependent' condition (`sa.dependent`), both refused in scope (`dependent.divorced_rule` refuses the entry; `sa.dependent` refuses the standard deduction). Compared by sampling 40,000 inputs per line with every refusal trigger false and consistent answers (only a married person files a joint return; over half of a person's support cannot come from both the person and you): no difference on the child tax credit lines; the remaining differences on odc_person, odc_amount and hoh_test2 all come from the second treating `sibling_descendant` as a Step 4 relative, which the enum defines as any other descendant of a sibling (a Step 4 relative only as a household member who lived with you all year; i1040gi p. 19 lists only a son or daughter of a sibling, which is `sibling`), and from `other` living with you all year, which the all-year household bullet admits. No change.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope and representation; project retained. The second transcription folds the qualifying-child, dependency and credit tests into each line and omits the 'you can be claimed as a dependent' condition (`sa.dependent`), refused in scope (it refuses the standard deduction); the rule for children of divorced or separated parents is refused on the entry (`dependent.divorced_rule`). Stage 15 re-run: both sides now count a filer or spouse who has applied for an ITIN (`person.itin_applied`) in the joint-return identification test (household.all_tin). Sampling 40,000 inputs per line with every refusal trigger false (`dependent.other_claimant`, `.divorced_rule`, `.multiple_support`, `.married`, `.income_exception`, `sa.dependent`) and consistent answers (only a married person files a joint return; over half of a person's support cannot come from both the person and you): the only differences come from the second treating `sibling_descendant` as a Step 4 relative whatever the time lived with you, and from its excluding `other` living with you all year. i1040gi p. 19, Step 4, lists "Brother, sister, half brother, half sister, or a son or daughter of any of them (for example, your niece or nephew)" (which is `sibling`; the enum defines `sibling_descendant` as any other descendant of a sibling) and "Any other person (other than your spouse) who lived with you all year as a member of your household", which admits `other` living with you all year and admits `sibling_descendant` only on that footing, as the project does. No change.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. Both count a dependent who lived with you more than half the year, leaving out one who is your dependent only because they lived with you all year, and an unmarried qualifying child (i1040gi p. 14, Head of Household, Test 2, items 1, 1b and 2); items 1a, 1c, 3 and 4 are refused on both sides (the project through dependent.divorced_rule, dependent.multiple_support and dependent.married on the lines this one reads), and the project now carries the TIN refusal (dependent.claimed_no_tin; p. 22, 'You must enter each dependent's social security number (SSN)'). The second writes the same exclusions in its own structure.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope and representation; project retained. The second transcription folds the qualifying-child, dependency and credit tests into each line and omits the 'you can be claimed as a dependent' condition (`sa.dependent`), refused in scope (it refuses the standard deduction); the rule for children of divorced or separated parents is refused on the entry (`dependent.divorced_rule`). Stage 15 re-run: both sides now count a filer or spouse who has applied for an ITIN (`person.itin_applied`) in the joint-return identification test (household.all_tin). Sampling 40,000 inputs per line with every refusal trigger false (`dependent.other_claimant`, `.divorced_rule`, `.multiple_support`, `.married`, `.income_exception`, `sa.dependent`) and consistent answers (only a married person files a joint return; over half of a person's support cannot come from both the person and you): the only differences come from the second treating `sibling_descendant` as a Step 4 relative whatever the time lived with you, and from its excluding `other` living with you all year. i1040gi p. 19, Step 4, lists "Brother, sister, half brother, half sister, or a son or daughter of any of them (for example, your niece or nephew)" (which is `sibling`; the enum defines `sibling_descendant` as any other descendant of a sibling) and "Any other person (other than your spouse) who lived with you all year as a member of your household", which admits `other` living with you all year and admits `sibling_descendant` only on that footing, as the project does. No change.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope and representation; project retained. The second transcription folds the qualifying-child, dependency and credit tests into each line; it also lets the rule for children of divorced or separated parents stand in for residency and omits the 'you can be claimed as a dependent' condition (`sa.dependent`), both refused in scope (`dependent.divorced_rule` refuses the entry; `sa.dependent` refuses the standard deduction). Compared by sampling 40,000 inputs per line with every refusal trigger false and consistent answers (only a married person files a joint return; over half of a person's support cannot come from both the person and you): no difference on the child tax credit lines; the remaining differences on odc_person, odc_amount and hoh_test2 all come from the second treating `sibling_descendant` as a Step 4 relative, which the enum defines as any other descendant of a sibling (a Step 4 relative only as a household member who lived with you all year; i1040gi p. 19 lists only a son or daughter of a sibling, which is `sibling`), and from `other` living with you all year, which the all-year household bullet admits. No change. Stage 13 re-run: the second transcription now applies the joint-return identification rules as the project does (household.ctc_ssn, household.all_tin, household.all_work_ssn; i1040gi p. 17, Before you begin, and p. 40, Step 1, question 2).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope and representation; project retained. The second transcription folds the qualifying-child, dependency and credit tests into each line; it also lets the rule for children of divorced or separated parents stand in for residency and omits the 'you can be claimed as a dependent' condition (`sa.dependent`), both refused in scope (`dependent.divorced_rule` refuses the entry; `sa.dependent` refuses the standard deduction). Compared by sampling 40,000 inputs per line with every refusal trigger false and consistent answers (only a married person files a joint return; over half of a person's support cannot come from both the person and you): no difference on the child tax credit lines; the remaining differences on odc_person, odc_amount and hoh_test2 all come from the second treating `sibling_descendant` as a Step 4 relative, which the enum defines as any other descendant of a sibling (a Step 4 relative only as a household member who lived with you all year; i1040gi p. 19 lists only a son or daughter of a sibling, which is `sibling`), and from `other` living with you all year, which the all-year household bullet admits. No change.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope and representation; project retained. The second transcription folds the qualifying-child, dependency and credit tests into each line and omits the 'you can be claimed as a dependent' condition (`sa.dependent`), refused in scope (it refuses the standard deduction); the rule for children of divorced or separated parents is refused on the entry (`dependent.divorced_rule`). Stage 15 re-run: both sides now count a filer or spouse who has applied for an ITIN (`person.itin_applied`) in the joint-return identification test (household.all_tin). Sampling 40,000 inputs per line with every refusal trigger false (`dependent.other_claimant`, `.divorced_rule`, `.multiple_support`, `.married`, `.income_exception`, `sa.dependent`) and consistent answers (only a married person files a joint return; over half of a person's support cannot come from both the person and you): the only differences come from the second treating `sibling_descendant` as a Step 4 relative whatever the time lived with you, and from its excluding `other` living with you all year. i1040gi p. 19, Step 4, lists "Brother, sister, half brother, half sister, or a son or daughter of any of them (for example, your niece or nephew)" (which is `sibling`; the enum defines `sibling_descendant` as any other descendant of a sibling) and "Any other person (other than your spouse) who lived with you all year as a member of your household", which admits `other` living with you all year and admits `sibling_descendant` only on that footing, as the project does. The second's note (Step 5 question 1 applied to every ODC person) is how the project reads it too (household.all_tin in the expression). No change.
